svg.title: A 20-month-old is 1 day post-appendectomy. She winces and pulls away when her abdomen is touched, will not walk, and cries when repositioned but cannot describe her pain in words.
svg.desc: The FLACC scale is validated from 2 months to 7 years and scores observed behavior (face, legs, activity, cry, consolability), so it does not require the child to describe her pain, unlike the FACES or numeric scales which depend on reliable self-report starting around age 3. Predictable postoperative pain is managed with analgesics scheduled around the clock rather than given only in response to crying, because waiting for visible distress lets pain build and become harder to control, undertreating the child.
